week.lesson_title: "Let Every Thing That Hath Breath Praise the Lord"

days.focus_note: The Lord can comfort me in my suffering. Psalm 102:1–11 describes anxiety and isolation in trials; 102:12–28 and 103 shift to praise and confidence in God's mercy.
days.source_excerpt: Note how Psalm 102:1–11 describes feelings of anxiety and isolation that often come during challenges. Maybe you or others you know have experienced such feelings. As you read Psalms 102:12–28; 103; 116, look for phrases that give you confidence to "call upon the name of the Lord" in your trials (Psalm 116:13). You might want to mark, memorize, or share with others phrases that give you hope in Him. See also Isaiah 25:8; Hebrews 2:17–18; Alma 7:11–13; Camille N. Johnson, "Christ Is Relief," Liahona, May 2023, 81–83; "Where Can I Turn for Peace?" (Hymns, no. 129).

days.focus_note: Continuing the theme of calling on the Lord in trials (Psalm 116), then turning to how Jesus Christ fulfilled prophecies from the Psalms in Psalms 110 and 118.
days.source_excerpt: As you read Psalms 102:12–28; 103; 116, look for phrases that give you confidence to "call upon the name of the Lord" in your trials (Psalm 116:13). ... Psalms 110; 118 Jesus Christ fulfilled prophecies from the Psalms. The Psalms contain passages that point toward the life and ministry of Jesus Christ. Here are a few examples: Psalm 110:1–4 (see Matthew 22:41–45; Hebrews 5:4–10; 6:20); Psalm 118:22 (see Matthew 21:42; Acts 4:10–11; 1 Peter 2:7); Psalm 118:25–26 (see Matthew 21:9). What do these verses teach you about Jesus Christ? Why is it important to know this about Him?

days.focus_note: God's word will keep me on His path. Psalm 119 uses journey imagery—'walk,' 'path,' 'way,' 'feet,' 'wander'—to describe our path back to Heavenly Father.
days.source_excerpt: Psalm 119 God's word will keep me on His path. Psalm 119 contains many phrases that compare our lives to a journey back to Heavenly Father. As you read, look for words like "walk," "path," "way," "feet," and "wander." Ponder your own life's journey—where you have been, where you are now, and where you are heading. What do you learn from this psalm about your journey back home? ... According to this psalm, what has God provided to help you stay on His path? ... 'Thy word is a lamp unto my feet, and a light unto my path' [Psalm 119:105].

days.focus_note: The Lord is more powerful than any idol. Psalms 134–36 list the powerful things the Lord has done, contrasting with the foolishness of trusting false gods (135:15–18).
days.source_excerpt: Psalms 134–36 The Lord is more powerful than any idol. Notice why, according to Psalm 135:15–18, it is foolish to trust in false gods. What might you be tempted to trust in that is similar to an idol? You might make a list of the things the Lord can do, as the psalmists did in Psalms 134–36. What powerful things has He done for you?

days.focus_note: The Lord knows my heart. Psalm 139 emphasizes that God is fully aware of our thoughts, actions, strengths, and weaknesses.
days.source_excerpt: Psalm 139 The Lord knows my heart. What do you find in Psalm 139 that helps you understand that the Lord is aware of you—your thoughts and actions, strengths and weaknesses? How does this truth influence your life and your choices?

days.focus_note: 'Praise ye the Lord.' The final psalms are a call to praise, considering reasons and ways to praise God.
days.source_excerpt: Psalms 146–50 "Praise ye the Lord." As you read these final psalms of praise, think about reasons you have to praise the Lord. Why is it important to praise Him? What are some ways you can praise Him?
